title: Autonomous Agents Have Crossed the Production Threshold: 5 Lessons from Scaling to 10M Users
content:
Last year, agentic workflows were primarily proofs-of-concept. Today, our fleet of autonomous multi-agent workers executes 4.2 million asynchronous tasks every 24 hours.

Here are 5 counter-intuitive engineering architectural takeaways:
1. Deterministic state machines beat open-ended loops every time.
2. Small, specialized fine-tuned models outperform giant general LLMs by 3.4x in latency and 80% lower cost.
3. Human-in-the-loop validation is not a bottleneck; it is your training flywheel.
4. Observability and trace graphs are the new compiler debugging.
5. Prompt engineering has morphed into distributed systems engineering.

Are you running autonomous agents in production yet, or still prototyping?

title: Building Deep Learning Systems from Scratch: 10 Core Fundamentals Every Engineer Must Master
content:
If you only understand AI through API calls, you are vulnerable to model commoditization.

To build durable engineering leverage, dive into:
1. Tensor operations and CUDA memory coalescing
2. Backpropagation with automatic differentiation
3. FlashAttention-3 implementation internals
4. Quantization (FP8, INT4 AWQ) and KV-cache compression
5. Multi-GPU gradient accumulation and Pipeline Parallelism

Code first, buzzwords second.

author.name: Andrew Ng
author.info: Founder of DeepLearning.AI | Managing General Partner at AI Fund | Stanford Adjunct Professor

title: Prompting is Dead, Context Engineering is King
content:
If you are tweaking 50 adjectives in your prompt to get reliable JSON output, stop.

Context engineering consists of:
1. Dynamic in-context few-shot selection via vector cosine distance
2. Deterministic JSON schema validation with Pydantic & Zod
3. Recursive self-correction loops when grammar fails
4. State caching across turns to minimize token expenditure

Prompt engineering was 2023. Systems engineering is 2026.

title: Why We Switched 100% of Our Cloud Microservices to Rust: 12-Month Telemetry Report
content:
One year ago, our cloud AWS bill was $142,000/month across 85 Node and Python containers.

We ported the top 4 ingestion services to Rust.

The real production numbers:
• CPU utilization dropped by 74%
• Memory footprint reduced from 1.8GB per instance to 34MB
• p99 response times dropped from 240ms to 8.2ms
• Monthly infrastructure bill reduced to $38,000

The compiler fight during week 1 is worth the 10x leverage in year 1.
